newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond spreads unch, players eye new issues.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond spreads unch, players eye new issues.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were trading unchanged in quiet dealings, in line with U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.
Spreads to U.S. Treasuries were seen unchanged across most maturities, they added.
"Spreads are unchanged there were some insurance companies in buying this morning but by and large it's a very quiet day," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Meanwhile, players are focusing on next week's upcoming issues following a week that saw about $2.5 billion in new straight corporate debt.
Despite the billions in fresh supply this week, traders said no real spread deterioration was seen.
"It looks like spreads in general are about the same to maybe a basis point wider," another syndicate source said.
Turning to the primary arena on Friday, Coca-Cola Enterprises issued $250 million in 6.95 percent 30-year debentures to yield 63 basis points via lead manager UBS Securities.
Among upcoming issues CNA Financial is expected to issue $250 Millionin 10-year debt, syndicate sources said.
Rubbermaid is also expected to issue 10-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, sources said.
ABN-Amro (Chicago) is expected to tap the market with $300 million in A2/AA-minus rated 30-Year debt, sources added.
Dealers said with U.S. Treasury yields at their lowest levels in eight months new issues should continue to pour in as we approach year-end.
"I think we'll continue to see a big pick up in new issues through the end of the year if levels remain where they are," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Among other issues, JP Morgan Securities is expected to underwrite a $500 million 10-year and 20-year debt offering for Enersis SA, dealers said.
Turning to high-yield sector, Marvel Holdings Inc's "old" bonds gained 2-1/2 points to trade at a 24 bid without an offer, traders said.
"At the moment the paper is bid at 24, however, it looks like the offers are scurrying away," one high-yield source said.
"There are rumors in the market that a host of mutual funds have banded together to form an informal committee who are supposably rumored to be buying bonds," the source added.
Traders said last week Marvel paper was trading at a 25 bid but fell substantially by the middle of this week to trade at an 18 bid.
Marvel shares and debt sank on Tuesday after Andrews Group Inc offered to buy 80.1 percent of new Marvel common stock for $350 million, well below market costs.
The acquisition would be paid for in cash and/or Toy Biz Inc common stock.
Meanwhile, Marvel's stock was also buoyed by the market rumors, trading up 1/2 to 3-3/8.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
